options.text: The average speed of a single particle
Only the stored energy in a material
The total kinetic and potential energy of all the particles in a material
The temperature shown on a thermometer

items.explanation: Thermal energy is the sum of the kinetic and potential energy of all the particles that make up a material.

items.stem: Temperature is a measure of which of the following?

options.text: The total energy of every particle in an object
The average kinetic energy of the particles
How much matter an object contains
The amount of heat stored in an object

items.explanation: Temperature represents the average kinetic energy of the particles in a material. It tells you how fast they move on average, not how many there are.

items.stem: In what direction does heat always move?

options.text: From a warmer object to a cooler object
From a cooler object to a warmer object
From the larger object to the smaller object
It moves in no particular direction

items.explanation: Heat is the movement of thermal energy from a warmer object to a cooler one. It keeps flowing until both reach the same temperature.

items.stem: You hold a cool square of chocolate and it melts. What best explains why?

options.text: Cold energy leaves the chocolate and enters your hand
The chocolate creates its own heat and warms up
Your hand and the chocolate are exactly the same temperature
Thermal energy moves from your warmer hand into the cooler chocolate

items.explanation: Your hand is warmer, so thermal energy flows from your hand into the cooler chocolate. The added energy speeds up the chocolate's particles until it melts.

options.text: Heat carried by a moving liquid or gas
The transfer of heat by direct contact
Heat that travels as waves through empty space
Energy that only the Sun can produce

items.explanation: Conduction is the transfer of heat by direct contact. Particles collide with their neighbors and pass energy along.

items.stem: Which material would be the best conductor of heat?

options.text: Copper
Styrofoam
Cork
Trapped air

items.explanation: Most metals are good conductors, and copper is one of the best. Styrofoam, cork, and air are insulators that slow the movement of heat.

items.stem: Why is a foam cup a good choice for keeping a drink warm?

options.text: Foam adds new heat to the drink
Foam pulls cold into the drink
Foam is an insulator, so it slows the movement of heat
Foam is a metal, so heat passes through it quickly

items.explanation: Foam is an insulator. It slows the transfer of heat out of the drink, so the drink stays warm longer.

items.stem: A pot of water is heated on a stove. The warm water rises, the cooler water sinks, and a loop forms. Which method is this?

options.text: Conduction
Radiation
Insulation
Convection

items.explanation: This is convection, the transfer of heat by the movement of a liquid or gas. Warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, forming a loop that carries energy.

items.stem: Which statement about radiation is correct?

options.text: It can only happen inside metals
It transfers heat as waves and needs no matter to travel
It requires particles to touch and collide
It only occurs in liquids and gases

items.explanation: Radiation transfers heat as electromagnetic waves, such as infrared rays. Because it does not need matter, it can cross the empty space between the Sun and Earth.

items.stem: A camper feels warmth on their face from a campfire several feet away, even without touching it or standing in rising smoke. Which method best explains this warmth?

options.text: Conduction, because their face touches the fire
Convection, because smoke carries heat to their face
Radiation, because the fire sends out waves of energy
Insulation, because the air blocks the heat

items.explanation: The warmth travels as waves of energy from the fire to the camper's face. That is radiation, which moves heat without contact and without a moving fluid reaching them.
